# PaulGoodman
> Two halves in one repository: `fadden`, a builder that retrieves in-force Commonwealth tax legislation from the Federal Register and turns it into retrieval material, and `tax-radar-au`, a Rust binary running a synthetic provenance-first review queue that consumes a reviewed observation contract.

## Package overview
- **Repository**: https://github.com/ryanduguid/PaulGoodman
- **Version**: 0.4.0, released as the tag `v0.4.0`. Releases carry deterministic source archives built from Git with an SPDX 2.3 SBOM, `SHA256SUMS` and provenance attestations. They never carry a corpus or a builder wheel.
- **Licence**: releases 0.3.0 and earlier keep their Apache-2.0 or MIT licence for the code. Release 0.4.0 keeps FSL-1.1-ALv2 for the code; `main` and later releases are under the Ryan Duguid Public Attribution Licence 1.0, the FSL-1.1-ALv2 text with a public attribution condition (`LICENSE`, `NOTICE`); each version from 0.4.0 also becomes available under Apache-2.0 2 years after it is made available. Generated corpus output is derived from the Federal Register's CC BY 4.0 material and carries its own source and licence records. The EPUBs embed the Commonwealth Coat of Arms, which the CC BY grant excludes, so the `dist` stage of the Rust `fadden` binary separates what may be redistributed from what may not.
- **Packaging**: the review queue is the standalone Rust binary `tax-radar-au` (crate `tax-radar-au` 1.0.0, built with `cargo build --locked --release`); its Python import package `tax_radar_au` was removed. The Python distribution keeps the name `tax-radar-au` and carries the builder, which is not published to PyPI and has no console script; it runs as `python -m fadden <stage>`.
- **Python**: the development checkout requires 3.14 or later. Tests run on Python 3.14 and 3.15 on Ubuntu, plus Windows 3.14 coverage for the supported live-evidence export boundary. The radar's Rust tests, Clippy and formatting run on Ubuntu and Windows.

## Corpus builder (`fadden`)
- **Stages**: `discover`, `versions`, `download`, `probe13`, `retry13`, `extract`, `pii_scan`, `pii_scan2`, `finalize`, `rates`, `check_current`, `dist`, `dist_verify`, `export_monitor_contract`, `export_publication_bundles`, `capture_register`, `export_live_evidence_bundles`, plus the separate `rulings`, `as_at`, `compare_builds`, `search`, `authorities` and `witness` stages, and `quick`, which runs the fetch, build and index stages for a preset of 9 principal Acts. `BUILD.md` documents the order and the operating boundaries.
- **Deterministic output root**: no environment variable selects it. In a source checkout the generated files live under `./corpus/`; a deployed build uses the parent of the `build/` directory holding the stage modules.
- **Privacy gates**: `pii_scan` and `pii_scan2` run before `finalize`, which refuses to run without `pii_flagged.json`. Twelve titles are disciplinary registers naming private individuals.
- **ATO rulings (`rulings`)**: fetches up to 100 named ATO-authored Legal Database documents (rulings, determinations, practical compliance guidelines, decision impact statements and edited private advice) into paragraph JSONL with the ATO reuse notice. It never touches `./corpus/` and excludes any document that matches a personal-data pattern. Rows with a withdrawal notice stay in the output, and a run prints each notice with a warning that it may preserve reliance for an earlier period.
- **As-at check (`as_at`)**: classifies each captured compilation against a date. `captured` is not a finding that the text was the law on that date.
- **Build comparison (`compare_builds`)**: lists the sections added, removed and changed between two local builds, matched on container and section label. It compares the derived reading view, not the authorised text, and says nothing about an amendment's legal effect.
- **Rendition witness (`witness`)**: for the titles in `fadden/witness_sample.json`, compares the section identifiers `extract` yields from the EPUB with those the Register's Word rendition of the same compilation numbers, and writes each difference as a review item. Agreement on a sample is not proof that the extraction is correct.
- **Local search (`search`)**: indexes a finished corpus into one SQLite file (standard-library FTS5) after checking every row's provenance against `sources.json`, then answers full-text queries, defined-term lookups from definitions rows and section, Division and Subdivision cross-references, including the captured rulings that cite a section by its Act. Every hit carries its `row_id`, compilation and Register page; none of it is authorised text.
- **Dates in search (`search --as-at`)**: `query` and `define` return rows only from titles whose `as_at` status on the date is `captured`, and refuse the others by name with the status, the rows withheld and the next step. `cite-check --as-at` adds each cited title's status. `captured` is not a finding that the text was the law on that date, and the build holds one compilation of each title.
- **Draft check (`search cite-check`)**: reports how each citation in a draft resolves against one index, names the held sections either side of a section the build lacks, and grades a quotation in the citation's sentence against the section reached as `exact`, `normalised`, `partial` or `none`, or leaves it ungraded if nothing was compared; `search quote` grades one quotation against a row you name. A held quotation also reports how many other rows hold it. A grade shows what that row of the build holds, not that the provision applies or was the law at any date.
- **Authorities export (`authorities`)**: writes that build's sections of current Acts and captured ruling ids as the closed list for `gate --authorities` in DrDebits. A listed authority exists in the build; it is not thereby current or correctly applied.
- **Evidence contracts**: live Register capture, synthetic observations and publication candidates are distinct. A successful capture or export authorises nothing for publication.

- **Preset build (`quick`)**: `python -m fadden quick --out <empty folder>` builds and indexes 9 principal Acts locally, checks that each holds indexed rows, moves the build into that folder and prints the `AUS_ACCOUNTING_CORPUS_ROOT` setting for the MCP server's `search_tax_legislation`. One run on 6 November 2026 took 116 seconds on a Windows desktop PC, 90 of them the Crawl-delay. Nothing is downloaded from this project and nothing is published.

## Review queue (`tax-radar-au`)
- **Domain**: a synthetic, provenance-first review-queue demonstration over supplied Commonwealth tax-source metadata. It does not read or store source text.
- **Supplied metadata comparison**: compares a fabricated source index, a fabricated Register-observation contract and an exact source-to-workflow map. The queue itself makes no network request and never scrapes the Register.
- **Review evidence binding**: SHA-256 source digests, run identifiers and a complete queue digest bind a human decision to the exact queue reviewed.
- **Human in the loop**: it generates deterministic change candidates. It establishes no current law, legal effect, workflow update or client action.

## What talks to the network, and when
Documented network access is 7 builder stages that reach the Federal Register and `rulings`, which reaches the ATO Legal Database. The review queue itself makes no network request.
- `discover` waits 3 seconds after each keyword and collection query and 2 seconds between full pages; its request count depends on the matching titles, plus 1 request for the reviewed named titles in `docs/scope.md`. `versions` resolves up to 8 titles a request: for 946 titles with no ambiguous groups, 119 resolution requests plus 1 diagnostic, with 178.5 seconds of fixed pauses (`BUILD.md`).
- `download` fetches one EPUB per title through `curl`, sleeping 10 seconds between titles to honour the Register's `robots.txt` Crawl-delay. All 946 titles take about 2 hours 40 minutes, and titles already downloaded at the same version are skipped.
- `probe13` reads version history for the titles `download` recorded as `no_epub`, and `retry13` downloads the latest published compilation for those it can recover.
- `check_current` is a read-only staleness check: 946 API calls at 1.5 seconds, about half an hour.
- `capture_register` observes every title in a manifest against the Register and retains the exact bounded HTTP 200 response bytes behind each decision. The 946-title manifest needs at least 946 requests, an enforced 1.5-second gap makes a no-retry run about 24 minutes, redirects are refused, the socket timeout is 90 seconds and each title gets at most 3 attempts. No API key is required.
- `quick` makes no request of its own: it runs `versions`, `download` and, for a title with no published document, `probe13` and `retry13`, on its 9 Acts.
- `rulings` fetches only the named targets, one request a second, HTML only, at most 8 MiB a page, from `https://www.ato.gov.au`. There is no discovery crawl.
- `as_at`, `authorities`, `compare_builds`, `search`, `witness`, `extract`, `pii_scan`, `pii_scan2`, `finalize`, `rates`, `dist`, `dist_verify`, `export_monitor_contract`, `export_publication_bundles` and `export_live_evidence_bundles` make no request at all. The monitor and publication exporters project facts a caller has already collected.
